title: CSRF: the state-changing HTTP routes are protected by the Origin check plus a SameSite=Strict cookie, but the WebSocket upgrade checks no Origin, so any same-site page (another port on the same host name) can open /ws with the operator's cookie and read the live feed

evidence.note: handleUpgrade checks the path and the session cookie only; Origin is never read
server.on('upgrade', ...) bypasses the express middleware chain, so the CORS/Origin gate (server.ts:100-144) never runs for /ws

cookie sameSite strict: not sent from a cross-site page, but SameSite treats every port of the same host name as the same site (http://127.0.0.1:3000 and http://127.0.0.1:8080; localhost:5173 and localhost:8080)
HTTP: a cross-origin Origin is rejected with 403 before any route runs (loopback repro in AUD-API-005: Origin http://127.0.0.1:3000 -> 403)
what a hijacked socket receives: positions_update every 5 s, notifications (all Telegram alert texts), anti-rug events, pause and chain status

sibling_sites_checked: Every state-changing route (grep router.post over the snapshot): controls.ts force-sell, emergency-sell, pause, resume; chains.ts stop, start; antiRug.ts CB reset; auth.ts login. All are POST behind the Origin gate; no GET route changes state (the GET routes are read-only, trades export included). A form or fetch POST from another origin carries an Origin header in current browsers and is refused before the route; a cross-site page also lacks the Strict cookie. The WebSocket has no inbound message handler (no ws.on('message') in src/api), so a hijacked socket can read but not command; a browser cannot send the malformed frame that crashes the server (AUD-API-009). The configured DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS list (server.ts:133) intentionally opens HTTP to listed origins.
severity_rationale: S3 EXPOSURE: read-only disclosure of the whole live trading feed to a page on the same host name (for example a local dev server or another local web app the operator opens), needing no credentials; no control path found for HTTP. Not run in a browser here (code reading).
recommendation: Check Origin on the WebSocket upgrade against the same allowlist as HTTP (and the Host allowlist from AUD-API-005); reject with 403. Card API-03. Phase 29.

sub_claims.claim: HTTP state-changing routes reject requests with a cross-origin Origin before the route runs (no HTTP CSRF gap found)
The /ws upgrade accepts any Origin and a same-site page receives the Strict cookie
